column1: # One row per conformance check. Columns (tab separated):
#   check  part  requirement  scenarios (separated by " | ")  fault  capability
# A check's fault is a named break of the in-memory event loop (memory.goose, set_fault) that makes the check fail; the column may
# hold several, separated by commas, and the check must fail under each.
# A check with an id of 900 or more (finished_loop and its capability variants) runs after serve has returned, on the finished loop.
# The half-close and abort capabilities have no finished-loop check: their link operations return nothing, so their finished-loop cells
# are covered by the unit tests of tests/unit/memory_loop_test.goose and tests/unit/wrapper_loop_test.goose.
# The capability is the one the check belongs to (core, half-close, sizing, abort, inspection, batching, unix, relay, peek, revoke, wake, limits, name-resolution, shared-listen); "pending" is a check
# not yet assigned (tasks 4.2 to 4.4 of simplify-contract). "-" in the fault column means no fault can be injected in a queue-based event loop; the reason is in docs/event-loops.md.
